newsitem.title: UK: NWE straight-run fuel oil offered higher.
newsitem.headline: NWE straight-run fuel oil offered higher.

text.p: European low sulphur straight-run started the week offered higher in a quiet market and traders said lower avails were supportive and movement to the U.S. would further tighten the market.
One seller said he was offering at $105 for 0.5 pct sulphur material, which is $2 over late last week, but very few buyers were said to be in the market and no serious bids were heard.
But the seller said the buyers would probably come in the low three figures as they were at $99 when straight-run was on offer around the $012/$103 mark recently.

"It is being offered a little higher, availability is moving to the States and we were not really oversupplied. Maybe with two or three cargoes moving Stateside the market will tighten," the seller said.
It was not immediately known if a U.S. independent refiner that was looking for a cargo to top up three earlier ones going transatlantic was still on the market.
One Scandinavian refiner said he was not offering but will start talking his July 20 cargo by the end of the week.
Russian high sulphur straight-run was notionally assessed steady in a very quiet market, with most avails said to be M-100 cargoes.
"For prompt requirements there's not much E-4 on offer, only M-100," one trader said.

One trader said a cargo was on offer at two means +$3, the same price a cargo traded late last week, while a trader with a major said he was re-offering a cargo at a $2 premium to two means, but no serious bids came in.
